newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks dive on Kia Group troubles.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks dive on Kia Group troubles.

text.p: Seoul stocks opened sharply lower on Wednesday, battered by financial troubles at the Kia Group. All six listed Kia affiliates plunged, with four going limit-down, brokers said.
The composite stock index dropped 11.93 points or 1.58 percent to 743.12 in the first 20 minutes of trading.
Financial shares took the most severe beatings in early trading with the sub-index for the banking sector plunging 3.85 percent to 348.38.
The Korea First Bank, a main creditor of the troubled Kia Group fell 250 won to 3,250 by 0115 GMT. It briefly touched its daily limit of 3,220.
"Troubles with the Kia Group dampened sentiment dramatically. The impact will continue for the time being," said Lim Sung-woon, a broker at Daewoo Securities.
On Tuesday local banks decided to rescue the Kia Group whose carmaking flagship had been hit by slumping sales.
Kia's woes were compounded by persistent bankruptcy rumours.
A challenge by newcomer Samsung Motors, rumoured to be interested in buying Kia Motors as a short-cut into industry top ranks, added to a sense of crisis, analysts said.

The group's flagship carmaker Kia Motors, commercial vehicle producer Asia Motors, Kia Service and Kia Steel went limit-down, while investors were bidding at limit lows for Kisan and Kia Precision, the brokers said.
The Korea Stock Exchange halted trading in the six Kia companies on Tuesday afternoon.
